strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-29105 regression: np.percentile/np.quantile on a float32 array with np.float64 q returns float32 instead of float64 for interpolating methods. Build numpy from source at the buggy commit 437a350e2c87, apply the PR's test diff, and run the new TestPercentile/TestQuantile promotion tests. The fix is the PR's Python-level change in nanpercentile/_nanquantile_1d (deferring the cast via weak_q); the fixed revision hash is not in the evidence, so the fixed checkout must be taken as the PR merge commit.

pinned_because: none pinned: pytest, hypothesis and numpy have no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the context, so the latest versions compatible with the checked-out source are used and this choice is stated, not inferred from evidence
numpy is the checked-out revision itself, built in place, so its version is the commit, not a pip pin

strategy.test_command: python -m pytest numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py -k 'test_q_strong_promotion or test_q_weak_promotion' -q -p no:cacheprovider
strategy.reproducing_test: numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py::TestPercentile::test_q_strong_promotion[all interpolating methods] and numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py::TestQuantile::test_q_strong_promotion[all interpolating methods]; test_q_weak_promotion is a control that should pass on both revisions
strategy.success_criterion: Buggy 437a350e2c87 with the test diff applied: every test_q_strong_promotion case for the interpolating methods fails with AssertionError because value.dtype is float32 where float64 is asserted, in both TestPercentile and TestQuantile; test_q_weak_promotion passes. Fixed revision: test_q_strong_promotion passes for all interpolating methods (float64 result), and test_q_weak_promotion still passes (float32 result). The transition is the pass/fail change of the strong-promotion tests.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import numpy as np; print(np.percentile(np.ones(10, dtype='float32'), np.float64(3)).dtype)"
risks: The discrepancy is a dtype difference, not a value difference; the test asserts dtype equality, so a value-based check would not separate buggy from fixed.
Only interpolating methods are covered by the test diff; method='nearest' (discrete) dtype is unresolved in the evidence and is not asserted by the test, so it must not be used as a pass/fail signal.
The fixed revision hash is not stated in the evidence; the transition requires checking out the PR merge commit, which must be identified separately.
Test patch must apply cleanly to 437a350e2c87; the module-level interpolating_quantile_methods list is inserted in the test file and the -k selector depends on those test names.

Platform: promotion logic is pure Python and not architecture-dependent in the evidence, so no special platform is assumed; the numpy build still needs a working C/C++ compiler and meson/ninja toolchain, which the evidence does not specify.
Longdouble inputs previously used higher precision for q; this side effect of the fix is not tested here and is not a pass/fail condition.
Hypothesis and pytest are unbounded in the context; a version mismatch with the test file's imports is possible but not evidenced.

oracle.reference_source: the PR test diff in numpy/lib/tests/test_function_base.py (dtype assertions)
oracle.why: The test checks value.dtype equality against np.float32 or np.float64, not numerical values, so an exact dtype comparison is the oracle; no tolerance is stated in the evidence.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On 437a350e2c87 np.percentile/np.quantile of a float32 array with np.float64 q return float32, so assert value.dtype == np.float64 raises AssertionError for each interpolating method parameter.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the result dtype is float64 for np.float64 q, so the strong-promotion assertions hold for all interpolating methods; the weak-promotion control still asserts float32 and passes.
